paper_metadata.title: Postconcussion Symptoms After an Uncomplicated Mild Traumatic Brain Injury in Older Adults: Frequency, Risk Factors, and Impact on Quality of Life

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses convenience sampling from a single medical center, which limits generalizability. While inclusion/exclusion criteria are clear, the lack of information on the total number of eligible non-participants makes it impossible to determine the participation rate or potential selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Participants who met the following criteria were included in our study: (1) 65 years and older, (2) confirmed diagnosis of a TBI with an initial Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 13 to 15...
items.reasoning: The target population (older adults with mTBI) is clearly defined by age and clinical severity markers.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: convenience sampling was applied to include participants in the emergency department and neurosurgical clinics of a medical center in northern Taiwan
items.reasoning: The setting is described, but convenience sampling is inherently prone to bias, and the flow of patients from identification to enrollment is not detailed.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between November 2019 and October 2020.
items.reasoning: The specific dates for recruitment are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were excluded if they or their family had reported more than 1 TBI prior to the study or if they sustained a second head injury during the study period. Participants diagnosed as having dementia, cognitive impairment, or psychiatric disorders before their head injury... were also excluded.
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical and demographic inclusion/exclusion criteria are provided, including 'zero time' (head injury event).

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 summarizes the demographics and disease characteristics of the study participants. Participants had an average age of 76 years, and the major cause of head injuries was falling (80.2%).
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of age, sex, education, GCS, LOC, and comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study maintained a very high follow-up rate (97%), which is well above the 80% threshold. The reasons for the few dropouts were provided and do not suggest informative censoring that would bias the prognostic relationship.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Overall, 101 participants with mTBI were included in the current study. A total of 3 participants withdrew from the study in the sixth month.
items.reasoning: 98/101 (97%) completion rate is excellent for a 6-month longitudinal study.

items.evidence_snippet: The primary reasons for withdrawal were sustaining another head injury and lack of time for participation.
items.reasoning: Specific reasons for the 3 withdrawals are clearly stated.

items.reasoning: The mCCI is a well-defined, standard prognostic tool in geriatric research.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes (PCS and QoL) were measured using internationally recognized, validated scales (RPQ and QOLIBRI). The timing of assessments was standardized.

items.evidence_snippet: The measurement tools were the Rivermead Post-Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire and the Quality of Life after Traumatic Brain Injury. Measurements were performed on the seventh day, at the first month, and at the sixth month
items.reasoning: Both outcomes and the follow-up schedule are explicitly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: The QOLIBRI was translated into the Chinese version in 2014, and has acceptable reliability and validity.
items.reasoning: The authors use validated versions of the RPQ and QOLIBRI, citing specific validation studies.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
